sources.quote: The most common supplement type was 30-day, at 7250 (67.3%), while PTS was least common, making up 132 (1.2%) of all supplements.
sources.searcher_note: All PMA devices approved 2008-2019, supplements through 2021: 30-day notices are 67.3% of supplements, near the lead's 64% for 2010 on. No early-2000s comparison, no P980016.

sources.quote: Excluding 30-day notice supplements, which have increased markedly since their introduction in 1997, there was still a 3-fold increase over the past decade, from 60 supplements to 194.
sources.searcher_note: Cardiac implant devices only (pacemakers, ICDs), 1979-2012: says 30-day notices rose markedly since 1997. Subset of the lead's device universe; direction matches.

sources.quote: These PMAs were the subject of 5829 PMA supplement applications. Nearly half (2754, 47%) were approved as 30-day notice supplements for manufacturing changes.
sources.searcher_note: Same study: 47% of cardiac-device supplements 1979-2012 were 30-day notices. Earliest source found on 30-day-notice share. Does not break out Medtronic P980016.

sources.quote: The study found that the most-used supplement type is a 30-day notice, used when a company makes changes to a manufacturing procedure or the way it makes a device.
sources.searcher_note: Trade-press write-up of the 2023 JAMA Network Open study; no share-over-time figure.

sources.quote: Almost all, 99%, of the supplements were filed without clinical data.
sources.searcher_note: Trade press on the same 2023 study; frames supplements as changes made without clinical data, tied to ~30% higher recall risk.

sources.quote: Two brands of cardiac defibrillator leads (Sprint Fidelis [Medtronic] and Riata [St Jude Medical]) were recalled after being approved by supplements due to high rates of lead failures.
sources.searcher_note: Closest Medtronic-defibrillator mention found: the Sprint Fidelis lead, not the P980016 ICD line the lead names.

notes: Academic literature covers the 30-day-notice share: Rome et al. JAMA 2014 (cardiac devices, 47%, 'increased markedly since 1997') and Dubin et al. JAMA Netw Open 2023 (all PMA devices 2008-2021, 67.3%). No source found giving the lead's specific 19% (2000-04) to 64% (2010 on) comparison across all PMA devices. No press or research source found naming Medtronic P980016 or its 928/621 counts; searches for P980016 returned only FDA approval letters (primary records, not coverage). ICIJ Implant Files covers the supplement pathway and Sprint Fidelis generally; the ICIJ pages fetched did not contain a quotable 30-day-notice sentence. No source found disputing the rise; FDA guidance describes the 30-day notice as the statutory route for manufacturing changes. PubMed and PMC pages returned reCAPTCHA; Harvard DASH thesis returned 405. No July-September 2026 coverage found.
